en.html: ...I seemed to have lost consciousness. One instant, perhaps two. In that time, the world had changed. First, my body was limp. No strength anywhere—my knees were on the ground, and I could not lift them. Ichijou was nowhere to be seen. Responding to my will, Muramasa used her ears...◆ There. Roughly four kilometers east-northeast. Four kilometers. Apparently she had been blown that far. ...So the scanner told me. Strange. Ordinary scanning sends a signal out, receives it after it strikes objects and returns, and thus surveys the surroundings. On the ground, too many objects interfere. Usually it cannot function. Yet it did. Actually, nothing strange about that. Even on the ground, signal scanning works perfectly well in the middle of a vast plain. That was all.
en.text:
...I seemed to have lost consciousness.

One instant, perhaps two.

In that time, the world had changed.

First, my body was limp. No strength anywhere—my knees were on the ground, and I could not lift them.

Ichijou was nowhere to be seen. Responding to my will, Muramasa used her ears...◆

There. Roughly four kilometers east-northeast.

Four kilometers.

Apparently she had been blown that far.

...So the scanner told me.

Strange. Ordinary scanning sends a signal out, receives it after it strikes objects and returns, and thus surveys the surroundings. On the ground, too many objects interfere. Usually it cannot function.

Yet it did.

Actually, nothing strange about that. Even on the ground, signal scanning works perfectly well in the middle of a vast plain.

That was all.

ja.html: ……俺は、気を失ったらしい。 　おそらく……一瞬か二瞬のことだったと思う。 　その間に世界は変容していた。 　まず、俺の全身は萎えている。 　まるで力が入らない――地面に落ちた膝は全く持ち 上がらない。 　一条の姿は何処にも見当たらなかった。 　俺の意思に反応した村正が探査機能みみを働かせる……◆ いた。東北東に約四キロの地点。 　四キロ・・・。 　つまりはそれだけの距離を吹き飛ばされたらしい。 　……探査機能がそう伝えている。 　不思議なことだった。信号を発信、物体に衝突して 戻ってくるそれを受信することで状況掌握を行う通常 探査は、地上では物が多過ぎるためまず機能しない。 　それが機能する。 　実は、不思議でも何でもなかった。地上であっても、 それが大平原・・・のど真ん中であれば信号探査は支障なく 機能するのだ。それだけの事だ。

en.text:
Only Silver Star remained unchanged in that transformed world.

Whatever it had done during the upheaval, no trace remained. A punch? A kick? A sweep of the sword? Nothing left from which to tell.

Perhaps it had done nothing. Perhaps its stillness meant simply that it had never moved.

Perhaps it had merely—◆become angry.

en.html:
Its furious words became blades, gouging my chest. Deeply. Painfully enough to imagine the taste of blood.

Why did they strike so deeply? Only the selfish pronouncements of a slaughtering monster. Nothing more.

Ichijou and I together could remove needless victims. Overcome Muramasa's curse, which demanded innocent lives. Only those the girl judged evil would die. That girl, more sincere than anyone in seeking human rightness, more rigorous than anyone.

How was that wrong?

What reason was there to abuse it?

........................And yet.

Perhaps I was so miserably shaken because, somewhere beyond my conscious thought, I already knew that reason existed.

Hikaru"Provided they are guilty, you may have someone else kill them. Have I understood you?"

Kageaki"In that... I do not see a wrong."
Hikaru"Ah. Now we have it."

en.html:
Hikaru"What is this talk? Those who should die are the weak. Those who should live are the strong."
Hikaru"Dying when one should not? There is no such person. Someone falls to your blade: someone has lost the contest of Arms. That is what has happened."
Hikaru"Good person, evil person—it makes no difference to that law. Death follows by reason. Where has any injustice entered?"
Kageaki"No...! Only evil that no judgment short of death can reach should die."
Kageaki"...But let Muramasa judge that evil, and an innocent has to die along with it. By the Balance of Good and Evil..."
Kageaki"That... I cannot accept."
Hikaru"Kageaki. Kageaki."
